get.description: Every medication you can order in the current mode, A to Z by name, then by ID. Send query to find medications by name: every word must appear in the name, so check the spelling when nothing matches. Then choose by name, strength, form and pharmacy. Send practiceId to list what that practice can order, at its prices; without it, the caller's organization is used. Prices are in cents. `requirements` names the optional prescription fields this pharmacy requires; `compoundingReasons` and `quantities` list the accepted values when the pharmacy limits them, counted in `quantityUnit`. With a `fill`, `price` is per fill and each quantity counts `quantityUnit`, not fills: it is a whole number of fills in units. For a fill of 30 tablets, quantity 60 is two fills. For vials, quantity 1 is one vial and quantity 2 is two vials. A 2 mL vial lists quantities 1–10; its volume is separate from its quantity.

post.description: One request creates the order, signs it and sends it to the pharmacy. Platforms must send practiceId; practice callers can omit it to use their own practice. With an API key, name the prescriber and send signatureAttestation. Optional prescriber phone and address each default to the practice; no account is looked up by NPI. In the app, the signed-in member signs with the NPI in their settings, or names the prescriber with the same attestation. With patient.id (a pat_ ID) or patient.externalId, the order reuses that patient of the practice and mode and updates the saved record; without them, each order creates a new patient. If id and externalId identify different patients, the request returns 422 invalid_order. When the pharmacy already holds the patient's name, a different firstName or lastName returns 422 invalid_order. Live orders require Live access on the practice and its platform. No payment method is required.
post.summary: Create, sign and submit an order

parameters.name: query

schema.description: Search saved order snapshots: patient names, email, phone and external ID; order external ID; prescriber name and NPI; medication names and brands; pharmacy name. Whole ord_ and pat_ IDs and six-character order numbers also match. Text matches ignore case and allow substrings, word prefixes and similar spellings for alphanumeric words of four or more characters. Every one of the first eight words containing letters or numbers must match; punctuation-only words are ignored. An empty or punctuation-only query leaves the list unfiltered. Date of birth, separate strength fields, practice names, prac_ IDs and rx_ IDs are not searched. Restart pagination when filters change.

post.description: 200 with status cancelled when the cancel is confirmed. 202 with cancelRequestedAt when the pharmacy has not confirmed yet: you get order.cancelled when it confirms, or, when it refuses, cancelRequestedAt becomes null and you get order.updated. If an earlier ask may have reached the pharmacy, a refusal keeps cancelRequestedAt and sends no event until the pharmacy ends the order (order.cancelled or order.shipped). 409 cannot_cancel when the order is shipped, delivered or failed. 409 cancel_refused when the pharmacy refused the cancel, or when Affinity could not reach the pharmacy; only the second says to retry with a new Idempotency-Key.

patch.description: `liveEnabled` allows or refuses new Live orders. Existing records, cancellation, webhooks and billing keep working. Only its platform changes it; enabling requires platform Live access, and either change needs a Live caller: a Live key (403 live_key_required otherwise) or a session in Live mode (403 live_mode_required otherwise). Live orders send `name`, `phone` and `address` to the pharmacy, so a practice with Live access changes them only in Live mode, with a Live key or a session in Live mode (403 live_mode_required otherwise). A retry with the same key and body returns the stored first response, even if the practice has changed. Use GET /v1/practices/{practiceId} to read the current practice.

post.description: Platforms and independent practices can register up to 16 public HTTPS endpoints per mode. An API key acts only for its own organization and mode. Every event goes to every endpoint. The signing secret is returned by creation and its idempotent replay for 24 hours.

Affinity POSTs each event as JSON to your registered endpoint URL, with an `Affinity-Signature: t=<Unix time in seconds>,v1=<signature>` header and an `Affinity-Event-Id` header that holds the event `id`. The signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of `t`, a period (`.`) and the raw request body bytes, keyed with the endpoint's whole signing secret (`whsec_…`). Verify each request before you use it: calculate the signature from the raw body, compare it with `v1` in constant time, and reject the request if they differ or if `t` is more than 300 seconds from your current time. Any 2xx response within 10 seconds acknowledges the delivery. Affinity does not follow redirects. After any other status, a redirect or no response, Affinity retries an order event, up to 12 tries in all, waiting 2, 4, 8 minutes and so on, at most 24 hours, between tries. A `webhook_endpoint.test` event is sent once and not retried.

post.description: Queue failed order event deliveries from the last 30 days for this endpoint. Only the current organization and mode apply. Each failed delivery gets up to 12 new attempts. Also make pending deliveries waiting on a later retry due now, without resetting their attempt counts. Keep the same event IDs, payloads, and per-order delivery sequence. The queued count includes both kinds. Pending deliveries already due, delivered events, and one-time test events stay unchanged. Send a unique Idempotency-Key for each request. Reuse that key after an uncertain response to return the original count. A request with a new key returns 0 when no eligible failures or pending deliveries waiting on a later retry remain.

practiceId.description: Required with a platform API key. Send a child practice ID. Independent practice keys can omit this field to use their own practice.

prescriptions.description: The 1 to 20 prescriptions approved for this patient.

optionId.description: The shipping option identifier from the medication's shippingOptions.

signatureAttestation.description: Must be true to attest that the named prescriber approved and signed these prescriptions.

ShippingDestinationInput.description: Defaults to the patient's address. State restrictions and pharmacy coverage use the destination's state.

line2.description: The apartment or suite, or null when there is none. Empty text, N/A, NA, none and - count as null. See notes, TBD and unknown return 422.

state.description: The two-letter US state or territory code, such as TX, in any letter case. Affinity stores and returns it in upper case.

postalCode.description: The US ZIP code: 78701, or ZIP+4 as 78701-1234, 78701 1234 or 787011234. Affinity stores and returns 78701 or 78701-1234.

compoundingReason.description: One of the medication's compoundingReasons values, required when the medication's requirements include it. Another value returns 422. Empty text counts as null.

directions.description: The prescriber's directions for use, as the clinician wrote them. None, N/A, NA, TBD, unknown and see notes return 422.

medicationId.description: The medication's public identifier from the current catalog.

notes.description: The prescriber's additional notes to the pharmacy. Empty text counts as null.

quantity.description: The prescribed quantity in quantityUnit, not a count of fills. With a fill, send a whole number of fills in units: two fills of 30 tablets is 60. A vial's unit is vial, so 2 is two vials.

refills.description: The number of authorized refills in addition to the first fill.

substitutionPermitted.description: Whether the prescriber permits substitution; defaults to true when omitted.

phone.description: A US phone number: 10 digits, with or without +1 or 1 before them. Spaces, dashes, dots and parentheses are allowed, such as (512) 555-0100. Affinity stores and returns +15125550100. Empty text counts as null. When the phone is omitted, null or blank, the order uses the practice phone.

npi.description: The prescribing clinician's 10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI). Surrounding spaces are removed.

PrescriberInput.description: Required with an API key. Send the prescribing clinician's NPI, firstName and lastName. Session callers can omit this field to sign with their own profile.

display.description: The reported allergy name. A whole-value no-allergy statement (NKDA, NKFA, none, unknown, denies, no, N/A and the same kind of phrase) returns 422, ignoring case, dots, hyphens, slashes, spaces and a trailing period. Send `[]` instead.

allergies.description: The reported allergies. Send `[]` when the patient reports no new allergies.

dateOfBirth.description: A real calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format, with a year from 1900 through 2099, today or earlier in UTC. Surrounding spaces are removed.

firstName.description: The first name. N/A, TBD, unknown and none return 422.

sex.description: The patient's sex as sent to the pharmacy.

lastName.description: The last name. N/A, TBD, unknown and none return 422.

middleName.description: The patient's middle name, or null when there is none. Empty text counts as null.

phone.description: A US phone number: 10 digits, with or without +1 or 1 before them. Spaces, dashes, dots and parentheses are allowed, such as (512) 555-0100. Affinity stores and returns +15125550100.

id.description: The pat_ ID of a saved patient of the order's practice, in the same Test or Live mode. The order reuses that patient and updates it from the sent fields. Send all other patient fields as usual. GET /v1/orders returns the patientId of each order. An unknown ID, or an ID of a different practice or mode, returns 404 not_found.
